Time-Lapse engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Time-Lapse rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app interval capture from product-page copy:

  • Camera Time-Lapse mode — Apple Camera feature that records frames at set intervals over a long period and assembles them into a short sped-up video. Labeled 延时拍摄, 延时摄影, or 延时视频 in zh-Hans system UI. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • Interval scheduling & frame sampling — capture logic that samples frames every few seconds or minutes and discards real-time playback. Your listing may mention interval capture or sped-up output; building sampling pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Sped-up video assembly & export — post-capture processing that stitches sampled frames into a playable timelapse clip at 24 or 30 fps. Listing copy explains those buyer benefits; timelapse sample video production is outside AppLocale scope.
  • AVFoundation & capture sessions — camera session code that runs for extended durations with power and thermal management. Entitlements and background capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Time-Lapse value to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Time-Lapse support in the binary.

A working Time-Lapse story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Time-Lapse vs Slo-Mo vs Cinematic Mode vs Action Mode vs Live Photos vs Panorama vs Burst — do not conflate

US/EU indie teams often merge ten Camera string families. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets Time-Lapse — long-duration recording compressed into a short sped-up video — not slow-motion playback, not cinematic video blur, not portrait background blur, not motion stills, not wide stitches, not rapid still bursts, and not low-light modes:

  • Time-Lapse & sped-up long recording (this page) — paragraphs and frame text explaining "Time-Lapse", "Time Lapse", "time-lapse video", "Sped-up recording", "Sunset timelapse", "Cloud motion", "Traffic flow", "Construction progress", "Night sky timelapse", 延时拍摄, 延时摄影, 延时视频, 延时记录. Hours of real time compressed into seconds of video.
  • Slo-Mo listing vocabulary (different) — high-frame-rate slow-motion playback of a short captured moment: Slo-Mo, Slow Motion, 慢动作, 慢动作视频. Slows time down — not speeds long recording up. Mention only as contrast — not the hero of this page.
  • Cinematic Mode listing copy (different) — shallow-depth cinematic video look with focus transitions: Cinematic Mode, 浅景深电影效果视频, 电影效果模式. Depth-of-field video storytelling — not interval timelapse marketing. Covered on our Cinematic Mode guide.
  • Action Mode listing copy (different) — extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage: Action Mode, 动作模式, 运动防抖. Video stabilization — not tripod-locked timelapse capture. Covered on our Action Mode guide.
  • Live Photos listing copy (different) — still photos with a few seconds of motion before and after the shutter: Live Photos, 实况照片, 动态照片. Motion stills — not hours-long sped-up video. Covered on our Live Photos guide.
  • Panorama listing copy (different) — wide horizontal or vertical stitched still photos while panning the phone: Panorama, 全景, 全景模式. Ultra-wide still stitches — not sped-up video over time. Covered on our Panorama guide.
  • Burst listing vocabulary (different) — rapid still capture in quick succession: Burst, Burst Mode, 连拍, 连拍模式. Many still frames at once — not interval sampling over hours. Mention only as contrast.
  • Night Mode listing copy (different) — low-light capture with longer exposure and computational blending: Night Mode, 夜间模式, 夜景模式. Low-light still photography — not sunset or star-trail timelapse marketing unless your English listing shows Night Mode timelapse specifically. Covered on our Night Mode guide.
  • Portrait Mode listing copy (different) — shallow depth-of-field still photography with soft background blur: Portrait Mode, 人像模式, 景深虚化. Subject-background separation — not timelapse video. Covered on our Portrait Mode guide.
  • Macro listing copy (different) — extreme close-up still photography at minimum focus distance: Macro, 微距, 微距近拍. Close-up detail shots — not landscape timelapse. Covered on our Macro guide.
  • Photographic Styles listing copy (different) — still-photo tone presets at capture: Photographic Styles, 摄影风格, 丰富对比度. Photo color grading — not sped-up video framing. Covered on our Photographic Styles guide.

Time-Lapse compresses hours into seconds. Slo-Mo stretches a short moment into slow playback. Cinematic Mode adds cinematic depth-of-field to video. Action Mode stabilizes handheld walking-running video. Live Photos adds motion around a still. Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Burst fires rapid stills. Night Mode brightens low-light shots. Portrait Mode blurs backgrounds on stills. Macro captures extreme close-ups. Photographic Styles adjusts tone at capture. Mixing vocabulary across those surfaces on one product page reads like confused localization — scope each screenshot frame to the workflow it actually shows.

Time-Lapse-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Sped-up-recording listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Time-Lapse feature — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Time-Lapse phrasing

US pages use "Time-Lapse", "Time Lapse", "time-lapse video", "Timelapse", "Sped-up recording", or "Capture hours in seconds." Apple's Simplified Chinese Camera vocabulary often uses 延时拍摄 for the mode toggle and general capture, 延时摄影 for creative timelapse photography positioning, and 延时视频 for the sped-up video output. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing timelapse capabilities your app does not support.

Interval vs sped-up output

Time-Lapse marketing often shows two distinct steps — interval recording in progress (timer, elapsed duration, frame counter) and finished sped-up playback (clouds racing, traffic flowing). Chinese buyers expect per-frame captions: 延时拍摄 for the mode toggle, 正在录制 for recording in progress, 延时视频 for finished sped-up output — not one generic "强大相机" string on every frame.

Use-case-specific demos

Sunset, cloud motion, traffic flow, construction progress, and night-sky star trails each signal different buyer intent. zh-Hans overlays should name the scenario the frame shows: 日落延时 for sunset timelapse, 云层流动 for cloud motion, 车流延时 for traffic flow, 施工进度 for construction progress, 星空延时 for night-sky timelapse — not English "Sunset timelapse" pasted through machine translation without context.

Do not conflate with Slo-Mo or Burst

Time-Lapse speeds long recording up into a short clip. Slo-Mo slows a short high-fps moment down. Burst captures many stills in rapid succession. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately — 慢动作 belongs on Slo-Mo frames, 连拍 belongs on Burst frames, 延时拍摄 belongs on timelapse frames.

Do not conflate with Cinematic Mode, Panorama, or Live Photos

Time-Lapse compresses hours into seconds of video. Cinematic Mode adds shallow-depth cinematic look to video. Panorama stitches ultra-wide stills while you pan. Live Photos adds a few seconds of motion around a still shutter moment. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need timelapse search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 延时拍摄, 延时摄影, and 延时视频 each signal different intent from Slo-Mo 慢动作 keywords or Panorama 全景 keywords.

  • Subtitle — one clause on timelapse or sped-up-recording outcome; room for 延时拍摄 or 延时摄影 within 30 characters — e.g. "延时拍摄，浓缩时光" or "延时视频，记录变化"

  • Description — lead with the interval-and-compress workflow; mention sunset, traffic, or construction use cases only when your app actually supports those scenarios or equivalent timelapse paths

  • Honest scope — if your app supports standard Camera timelapse only but not custom interval controls, zh-Hans copy should not imply pro interval scheduling unless your English listing already claims it accurately
